adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: National-framework reference that governs this region record under rule 1, since Kırklareli stands under Turkey's state law. Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since the Ottoman Empire adopted a new penal code in 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender (after surgery) since 1988. However, Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military, and same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition (no marriage, civil union, or adoption). Authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants; in ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking Turkey placed 47th out of 49 assessed countries. For this record: the legal protections a trans or LGBTQ visitor has (or lacks) are set entirely by this national framework; no Kırklareli-specific deviation is documented.
